verdicts.argument: I re-opened the other skeptic's pages and they hold. JNJ:10k_FY2025.md p.28 sets the -3.1 price line next to 'the negative impact of the STELARA sales decline ... approximately 6.2%'. p.37 lists 'the impact of Medicare Part D redesign' in the segment margin bullets. The 2025Q3 call p.6 says 'STELARA declined by 42%, driven by the impact of biosimilar competition and Part D redesign', and the 2025Q4 call p.6 says 'STELARA declined 48.6% ... biosimilar competition and Part D redesign'. My round 1 math still stands: -3.1 pts, about $2.75B, worst in six years, and the rebate leg shrinks to 0.6 pts against U.S. IM sales. But a material number with a named, recurring explanation is not a finding. The STELARA 6.2% covers both volume and price, so the filings cannot isolate any price erosion outside STELARA and Part D. The 10-Qs have no price/volume table, so a 2026 continuation cannot be tested either.
verdicts.correction: No finding as written. The only version that could be both material and non-obvious, price erosion outside STELARA continuing after Part D has lapped, cannot be built from the index.

round2.conceded: The drag is explained: STELARA biosimilars plus Part D redesign, named in the 10-K (p.28, p.37) and in prepared remarks on both 2025 calls. It is the starter thread, so I flip from held to refuted.
round2.held: The numbers are right on the page. The $2.75B and the six-year ranking hold, and the rebate-versus-sales gap is overstated (0.6 pts vs U.S. IM sales in 2025). Any rewrite must keep those corrections.
round2.narrowed: Only non-STELARA price erosion in 2026 would qualify, and it cannot be shown.

verdicts.argument: The other skeptic's pages check out. The deal is listed in the Q4 2025 earnings release (JNJ:earnings/2026-01-21_a2025q4exhibit991.md p.5). The 2026Q1 slides say 'Expect impact of voluntary agreement with the U.S. government to be evenly distributed throughout the year' (JNJ:presentations/2026Q1_earnings_slides.md p.23). At JPM the CEO answered a question about the agreement and called the tariff exemption the removal of 'an overhang' (JNJ:presentations/2026-01_jpm_fireside_transcript.md p.3). I/B/E/S FY2026 mean EPS went from 11.45 (2026-01-15, row 755) to 11.53 (2026-02-19, row 737) after the guide, so the 2026 cost is in consensus. Can the narrowed version (no terms disclosed, unlike BMS and Merck) be sized? No. Everything that sets the cost is confidential (press release p.1 footnote): products, term, discount depth, the TrumpRx channel. The only index data that bears on it is CMS Medicaid SDUD (data/moat/tables/medicaid_sdud.csv, all 4 quarters of 2025). It covers just 5 J&J drugs, with 2025 gross Medicaid reimbursement of about $2.6B: STELARA $1.37B, TREMFYA $0.53B, XARELTO $0.47B, DARZALEX $0.22B, RYBREVANT $0.01B. That is gross pharmacy reimbursement before the existing statutory and CPI rebates, for a partial product list. It is a loose partial ceiling on the Medicaid leg, not a size. My $0.12-per-1%-of-U.S.-IM-sales figure is a scaling unit with no anchor and should not be presented as an impact.
verdicts.correction: Keep only the disclosure gap: unlike BMS (free Eliquis to Medicaid, BMY 10-K p.19) and Merck (a named three-year term, MRK 10-K p.7), J&J discloses no products, term or discount depth. Say plainly that the out-year cost cannot be sized. The Medicaid leg for the 5 covered drugs is bounded only loosely, under about $2.6B gross before existing rebates.

pages_checked.page: stelara, tremfya, xarelto, darzalex, rybrevant rows, 2025

round2.conceded: The deal is guided, in the earnings release, discussed at JPM, and in consensus. 'No analyst asked' holds only for the four earnings calls. I flip to refuted.
round2.held: The cost is in the 2026 guide, so there is no EPS surprise for 2026. That was my round 1 point, and it now stands as the reason the EPS framing goes.
round2.narrowed: The disclosure gap alone cannot be sized. The index supports only a loose partial gross ceiling on Medicaid for 5 drugs (about $2.6B in 2025 before existing rebates), and nothing on TrumpRx or launch pricing.

verdicts.argument: I agree with the other skeptic that the IM plant drift (Item 2, p.23 in both 10-Ks), the Q2 2026 plant-exit program (10-Q p.35/p.48) and the January 20, 2029 sunset were never discussed on the calls. I re-checked 2025Q3 p.9 ('more manufacturing facilities in the United States than in any other country', all segments), 2025Q3 p.13 and 2026Q1 p.6 ('through early 2029', 22% of $55B spent). Is it material once my three corrections are applied? (1) Exposure base. The plant drift is one plant each way, and IM square footage and U.S. square footage both grew (p.23), so the drift has no P&L size of its own. Only the tariff scenario does. (2) Rate. At 15% the reader's arithmetic gives $0.86-1.20B. At the 20% rate for onshoring-plan companies (clause 3(b)), $5.8-8.0B x 20% = $1.15-1.60B, or $0.39-0.54 EPS after tax on 2,429.4M shares. That is 3.5-5% of the $11.10 2026 guide, and it falls to 100% only from April 2, 2030. (3) End date. Clause (3)(e) also applies the zero rate 'per the terms of the agreements listed in Annex II', and J&J's terms are confidential. So the scenario needs two things to happen: J&J's agreement not extending past January 2029, and the 'early 2029' U.S. build-out not covering U.S. demand. Neither probability can be anchored from the index. Conclusion: as a conditional exposure it is material, roughly $0.3-0.5 EPS a year. The plant count alone is not.
verdicts.correction: State it as a conditional risk. If the confidential exemption ends with the generic January 20, 2029 sunset and the $55B build-out is not finished, J&J faces about $0.9-1.6B a year pre-tax ($0.29-0.54 EPS) at 15-20% on an import share proxied by plant count. Neither condition is disclosed, and the 2025 shift (one plant each way) is the only hard fact.

round2.conceded: It is the least obvious item in the file. The IM split, the plant exits and the 2029 date are unsaid, and management's 'more U.S. facilities than any other country' counts all segments, which makes the IM split worth showing.
round2.held: The exposure base, rate and end date are all assumptions. The 2029 date may not bind J&J (Annex II, confidential terms), and the plant-count shift has no P&L size.
round2.narrowed: Material only as a conditional risk of $0.29-0.54 EPS a year at 15-20%. Range widened from round 1 to include the 20% rate. Not a forecast, not a bound.

verdicts.argument: I ran the peer check the other skeptic asked for. From December 2025 to June 2026, finished goods rose at J&J (7,833 to 8,405, +7.3%, JNJ:10q_2026Q2.md p.13) but fell at Merck (2,275 to 2,186, -3.9%, MRK:10q_2026Q2.md p.19) and Pfizer (4,113 to 3,887, -5.5%, PFE:10q_2026Q2.md p.21). So the H1 2026 build is specific to J&J, not industry-wide. On materiality my round 1 point stands. Finished goods J&J still holds do not pull revenue forward, so a 'later destock of sales' does not follow. The build is about $0.6B over the half year, and about $0.9B above a sales-paced level year over year. It matters for working capital and possible write-downs, not for revenue or EPS, unless a write-down is disclosed, and none is.
verdicts.correction: Keep as a minor watch item: J&J's finished goods rose 7.3% in H1 2026 while Merck's and Pfizer's fell. That is about $0.6B of working capital, with no revenue or EPS impact shown.

round2.conceded: The 2025 build is shared with AbbVie, so drop it, as the other skeptic said. The narrowed H1 2026 finished-goods build passes the peer check: J&J's rose while Merck's and Pfizer's fell.
round2.held: Finished goods on J&J's own balance sheet are not a channel or revenue risk. The candidate's 'revenue down' metric is wrong.
round2.narrowed: From major to minor: a real, J&J-specific working-capital item that is not material to earnings.

verdicts.argument: Confirmed on the 2026Q3 call p.6 (Ryan Koors, prepared remarks): 'Growth in other immunology is driven by IMAAVY and ICOTYDE launch uptake in the US.' The mapping to the 8-K line is therefore stated by management, and the $126M ceiling is a one-step read of 8-K p.11. Analysts asked on three calls running, and management said sales will be disclosed next year (p.14). My round 1 materiality points still apply. The line is about 0.5% of quarterly sales, and without a net price '$126M is little' cannot be shown.
verdicts.correction: No finding. A free-drug share estimate would need an ICOTYDE WAC, which the index lacks.

round2.conceded: Management states the mapping in prepared remarks and the question is asked every quarter. I flip to refuted.
round2.held: Even on materiality alone, the 'little revenue' inference is unsupported and the amount is small.

verdicts.argument: I accept the other skeptic's point that the price side appears in no J&J material and the label side is management's talking point (2025Q3 p.4, 2025Q4 p.4). But the narrowed claim fails on materiality. The four ASP rows are CMS table data (partb_asp_quarterly.csv lines 77, 81, 106, 110; values matched in pricing/sample_checks.csv). They have no page and cannot be quoted as page evidence. They cover only the IV induction vial in Medicare Part B. Most of the fall came between the 2025Q4 and 2026Q2 files (75.972 to 67.813), and the price has been flat since (66.920 in 2026Q3, 66.998 in 2026Q4). The reader's own sizing is $35M per point on U.S. TREMFYA (10-K p.89), about 0.04% of revenue. Even that applies the IV-vial move to SC/Part D sales, where the net price is not public.
verdicts.correction: If kept at all, keep it as a minor footnote cited to the CMS file and line: TREMFYA IV Part B payment limit -11.8% vs Skyrizi -6.2% (2025Q4 to 2026Q4 files), with the decline flat since mid-2026. It is not a material pricing finding.

round2.conceded: The price angle is non-obvious, and the label edge should come out of the finding text.
round2.held: It is immaterial and rests on unquotable machine data from a non-representative IV vial.
round2.narrowed: The decline is a one-time step that has been flat since the 2026Q2 file, not a running trend.

verdicts.argument: Confirmed: the CEO pitched the roll-off in Q&A, 'further amplified when the US. DARZALEX royalties roll off in 2029' (2026Q1 p.11, read in round 1). I/B/E/S FY2028 mean EPS is 14.25 (row 793, 2026-08-20). My numbers still hold: $2.4B, 12-20% and the 2029 U.S. expiry are on 10-K p.8, and the impact is about $0.45-0.47 EPS with the full year in 2030. But a material upside that management sells as a bull point is not an unsaid finding. The new piece of information, the $2.4B dollar figure, only sizes a date already announced. Xoma stays small: $52M per royalty point on $5,155M TREMFYA sales (p.89, p.109), about 0.06% of revenue per point.
verdicts.correction: Drop the Genmab roll-off. If anything is kept, it is the Xoma suit as a minor footnote risk (about $52M a year per royalty point), not material.

round2.conceded: The CEO pitched the roll-off on a call. I flip to refuted.
round2.held: The math ($0.45-0.47 EPS with 2030 as the first full year) is right and should be used wherever the roll-off is mentioned elsewhere.
round2.narrowed: Xoma survives as non-obvious but not material.

verdicts.argument: The other skeptic held it as non-obvious but raised the same lapping explanation I did. The 2026Q1 slides p.16 confirm 'unfavorable patient mix' wording across IMBRUVICA, STELARA and SIMPONI/REMICADE. On materiality nothing changes. The $119M rests on one quarter (U.S. H1 2026 was +10.2%, 10-Q p.26), compares U.S. growth with international growth that includes FX, and is about 0.13% of revenue. Their XARELTO test, 'favorable patient mix' in 2026 after 'Part D redesign' in 2025 (10-Q p.40; 10-K p.31), is the one place the relabel may be more than a lap. But XARELTO is not sized anywhere in the candidate, and the index gives no Medicare/commercial split to test it.
verdicts.correction: At most a disclosure-wording note with no dollar impact. The only testable thread is XARELTO's 2026 'favorable patient mix' under its first year of IRA pricing.

round2.conceded: It is unsaid, and the XARELTO case is a fair test of whether 'patient mix' still means Medicare channel.
round2.held: It is immaterial and the period logic (lapping) explains most of it.
round2.narrowed: From fatal to major: wording drift only. The XARELTO thread is open but unsized.

verdicts.argument: TREMFYA is material: 5.5% of FY2025 revenue (10-K p.8), with U.S. Q3 2026 sales +79.1% (8-K p.11). I accept the other skeptic's point that the SC-induction edge is management's own claim (2025Q3 p.4, 2025Q4 p.4) and that the CEO's '$10 billion-plus franchise' line is in prepared remarks (2026Q3 p.4). Their suggested alternatives are both immaterial on my lens: the IV ASP slide is about $35M per point, and Xoma is about $52M per royalty point.
verdicts.correction: The product choice is right on size, but no fine-print angle in the file is both material and non-obvious.

round2.conceded: The label edge is the company's own talking point.
round2.narrowed: The price and Xoma angles the other skeptic proposes are too small to carry the pick.

overall: After both lenses, nothing in JNJ is both clearly material and unsaid. The material items (price drag, MFN cost, Genmab roll-off) were all said by management, and the unsaid items (plant drift, IV ASP, finished goods, the 'patient mix' wording) are small or have no P&L size. The one exception is c03 as a conditional risk: if J&J's confidential tariff exemption ends with the generic January 20, 2029 sunset before its U.S. build-out lands, the cost is about $0.29-0.54 EPS a year, but neither condition can be anchored from the index.
